sections.html:
In Richland County one office decides what each parcel is worth (the auditor) and another sends bills and posts the money (the treasurer). Both are in the same Mansfield building, 50 Park Avenue East, ZIP 44902, open weekdays 8am to 4pm. The auditor's number is 419-774-5501 and the treasurer's number is 419-774-5622.

A third body, the Richland County Board of Revision, hears complaints about value. Its three statutory members are the auditor, the treasurer and the chair of the board of county commissioners, and each can appoint a stand-in. Value, exemption and complaint questions belong with the auditor. Balances, payment contracts and delinquency belong with the treasurer.

  • Auditor, 419-774-5501: valuation, Board of Revision complaint forms, owner occupancy and homestead applications, CAUV farmland.
  • Treasurer, 419-774-5622: bills, payments, payment contracts on real estate, and conveyance fee payments.
  • Sheriff's civil section, 419-774-3570: tax foreclosure and bank foreclosure sales.

Mansfield is the county seat, and the county has four cities (Mansfield, Ontario, Shelby and part of Galion), villages such as Bellville, Lexington and Shiloh, and 18 townships. Owners live in about 68 of every 100 homes.

The county's triennial update falls in tax year 2026, with the resulting bills payable in 2027. Ohio reappraises on a six-year cycle and updates values at the three-year midpoint without a physical inspection.

Three state reforms enacted in late 2025 also affect bills. House Bill 186 adds an inflation cap credit for districts at the 20-mill floor, and where it applies it shows up as a separate line on the bill. House Bill 335 holds inside millage growth to the rate of inflation in reset years. House Bill 129 changes the floor calculation beginning in tax year 2026. None of this ends property tax or freezes values.

sections.h2: How to file a Board of Revision complaint
sections.html:
File the complaint form with the Richland County Auditor, 50 Park Avenue East in Mansfield. The filing period runs January 2 through March 31, and there is no fee. Section 5715.19 allows filing until March 31 or the end of first-half collection, whichever is later, and counts the mailing postmark.

Call the auditor before filing, because a flawed complaint can be dismissed. Points to remember:

  • One complaint per parcel in a triennial period, unless the property sold, suffered a casualty or lost income. A complaint that was withdrawn still counts as the filing for that period.
  • Parcels can share a form only when they are contiguous or one economic unit, in the same taxing district, with identical ownership. When in doubt, file separately.
  • Attach the supporting documents you plan to use at the hearing when you file.
  • Hearing notice comes by certified mail at least 10 days out, and the hearing takes place in the auditor's office.

If the Board's written opinion still feels wrong, the next stops are the State Board of Tax Appeals and common pleas court.

Whoever files carries the burden of proof. Acceptable evidence reads like a checklist: comparable sales, a fee appraisal, itemized repair estimates, the closing statement and purchase contract after a recent sale, and income and expense records for rentals. Outcomes range from an increase to a decrease to no change.

Two limits matter to sellers. Sheriff's sales, bank sales, short sales and any sale where buyer or seller faced unusual pressure are not treated as arm's length, so they do not count as comparables. The Board also has no power over the tax rate, the percentage increase in a bill, the CAUV formula or the dollar amount of a bill, so a complaint that only objects to a higher bill goes nowhere.

Three common programs are handled through the auditor. Owner occupancy credit goes to the house you own and use as your main residence on January 1 of the filing year. Homestead exemption reaches owners aged 65 and up, owners with a permanent and total disability, and some surviving spouses. Most face an income test, but service-connected disabled owners do not. Ohio House Bill 96 of 2025 also lets county commissioners adopt a local-option homestead exemption equal to the state amount, which applies without a separate application if the county turns it on. Ask the auditor whether that local option is in place.

Farmland has its own track. Current agricultural use value, or CAUV, lets qualifying land be taxed on its farm value rather than market value. Ohio sets the qualifying bar at ten acres of commercial farming, or a smaller tract earning at least $2,500 a year in gross farm income on average. The formula averages seven years of data with the high and low years dropped.

Farm sellers should note that the buyer's conveyance statement must say whether the land carried CAUV status, and leaving the program can bring a recoupment charge.

sections.h2: Paying the bill and falling behind
sections.html:
Besides real estate, the treasurer takes personal property, mobile home and estate tax, and online card or eCheck payments carry a service fee. Real estate payment contracts exist for prepaying and for catching up. Ohio's default dates are December 31 and June 20, which counties may extend, and your bill shows the dates that apply.

A missed installment draws a ten percent penalty under section 323.121, and half of it is waived when the full amount arrives within ten days. Interest then accrues on delinquent taxes. The delinquent tax collector works with the county prosecutor on foreclosures, which is why an unpaid parcel can move from a bill to a court case.

While a valid delinquent tax contract holds, interest stops, and a breach brings back the interest that was paused. If you hold a contract and plan to sell, get the payoff in writing from the treasurer first.

Tax foreclosure sales, when scheduled, are held on Friday mornings at 10:00 in the training room of the Sheriff's Office at 597 Park Avenue East in Mansfield. The sheriff advertises each parcel in a newspaper beginning three weeks before the first sale, reads withdrawals aloud at the start of the sale, and requires the winning bidder to pay in full at the sale. A parcel that draws no sufficient bid can be offered again two weeks later at the same minimum price.

Bank foreclosure sales follow a separate path. To comply with Ohio House Bill 390, they are conducted only online through the sheriff's auction site. The Land Bank, on lower level 1 of the courthouse building, acquires vacant, abandoned houses to reduce blight.

An owner facing a tax judgment should call the treasurer's office at 419-774-5622 before the sale date to ask what payment, contract or sale the county will accept.

sections.h2: Selling when taxes are still owed
sections.html:
Get a written balance from the treasurer, then check it against the auditor's parcel record for the legal description, owner name and mailing address. The buyer's statement filed with the auditor discloses whether a tax reduction or CAUV status applied, and the seller covers the conveyance fee and any county transfer tax before the recorder sees the deed.

Line up three items early: the treasurer's payoff, the auditor's conveyance paperwork and tax map pre-approval for the deed. A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting, though the payoff and the transfer steps stay the same. Cash Home Buyers CA can walk through how the balance is paid from the proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: Which office answers questions about a tax bill?
faqs.a: The treasurer, at 419-774-5622, answers questions on amounts owed and payment contracts. The auditor, at 419-774-5501, handles value, exemptions and complaints. Both sit at 50 Park Avenue East in Mansfield.

faqs.q: When can an owner dispute a valuation?
faqs.a: From January 2 through March 31 each year, filed with the auditor at no charge. The statute lets the deadline run later when first-half collection closes after March 31.

faqs.q: Is 2026 a revaluation year in Richland County?
faqs.a: Yes. The triennial update occurs in tax year 2026, with taxes payable in 2027. State changes from House Bills 186, 335 and 129 are tied to those reset years.

faqs.q: Can selling the house stop a tax foreclosure sale?
faqs.a: Possibly, but ask first. Call the treasurer at 419-774-5622 for the judgment payoff and confirm timing with the sheriff's civil section at 419-774-3570.

faqs.q: Where is a deed recorded after a sale?
faqs.a: With the Richland County Recorder at 50 Park Avenue East in Mansfield. Tax map pre-approval should be included, and documents that need tax map and auditor review must be brought to the courthouse in person.
